newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN WIN TOSS, WEST INDIES TO BAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN WIN TOSS, WEST INDIES TO BAT.

text.p: Pakistani captain Wasim Akram won the toss and sent the West Indies in to bat in the first match of the final of the World Series limited overs competition at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Saturday.

The West Indies, who finished top of the table in the preliminary part of the competition, are favoured to win with key batsman Brian Lara in red-hot form and Pakistan without dashing opener Aamir Sohail.
Sohail was suspended for one match after being reported for dissent in Pakistan's loss to Australia on Thursday in the last game of the preliminary series.
Pakistan and West Indies qualified for the best-of-three series after host nation Australia were eliminated from the annual tri-nation competition last week for the first time since 1979/80.
Led by a resurgent Brian Lara, the West Indies have beaten Pakistan three times in their four games so far in the competition and have only lost one of their last six one-day matches.
However that loss was to Pakistan in their last match, also at the Sydney Cricket Ground, on Tuesday.
Pakistan should not take too much comfort from the result, given the West Indies had rested Lara and strike fast bowlers Curtly Ambrose and Courtney Walsh.
The West Indies are at full strength for this match, with the exception of spin bowler and middle-order batsman Carl Hooper, who has a shin injury.
Allrounder Phil Simmons, who only flew into Sydney on Friday, has been drafted in as Hooper's replacement.
Pakistan have replaced Sohail at the top of the order with free-swinging batsman and leg spinner Shahid Afridi.

West Indies - Sherwin Campbell, Junior Murray, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Phil Simmons, Jimmy Adams, Robert Samuels, Roland Holder, Ian Bishop, Curtly Ambrose, Courtney Walsh (captain), Cameron Cuffy (12th man).

Pakistan - Inzamam-ul-Haq, Shahid Afridi, Zahoor Elahi, Ijaz Ahmed, Mohammad Wasim, Mujahid Jamshed, Moin Khan, Wasim Akram (captain), Saqlain Mushtaq, Mushtaq Ahmed, Waqar Younis, Shahid Nazir (12th man).
